content.text: {"claims":[{"claim":1,"text":"Research on PostgreSQL streaming replication configurations for asynchronous log servers demonstrates that offloading write-intensive operations to dedicated servers can keep latency overhead below 4 percent at the same throughput level, with recommendations for institutions processing more than 400 transactions per second.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-01215","field":"abstract","quote":"the dedicated log server approach keeps latency overhead below 4 percent at the same throughput level"}]},{"claim":2,"text":"Work on append-only audit tables evaluated column-store systems against PostgreSQL using an 800 million record dataset, finding that column stores achieved storage reductions of 61–74 percent relative to the row-store baseline.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-01218","field":"abstract","quote":"a synthetic audit log dataset of 800 million records"}]},{"claim":3,"text":"Work on append-only audit tables found that range scan latency for twelve-month compliance report queries improved by factors of 4.2 to 7.8 when using column stores.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-01218","field":"abstract","quote":"Range scan latency for twelve-month compliance report queries improved by factors of 4.2 to 7.8"}]}]}
